findings.problem: The TL-01 answer sentence (action.answer, newPageBriefs[0].readerAndAnswer.answer, presented as the section 1 answer block) says the cap is 'the lesser of $50,000 (less any higher loan balance you carried in the past 12 months) or the greater of half your vested balance or $10,000, minus loans already outstanding'. The trailing 'minus loans already outstanding' attaches to the whole lesser-of and double-deducts outstanding loans from the $50,000 prong. Under 26 USC 72(p)(2)(A) the new loan plus all outstanding loans must not exceed min(50,000 - (highest12 - outstanding), max(vested/2, 10,000)), i.e. max new loan = min(50,000 - highest12, max(vested/2, 10,000) - outstanding).
findings.fix: Rewrite the answer in both places (they must stay identical) with the exact two-prong form, for example: 'Your new loan, added to loans you already owe the plan, cannot exceed the lesser of $50,000 reduced by how much your highest plan-loan balance in the past 12 months exceeded your balance today, or the greater of half your vested balance or $10,000; the calculator subtracts what you already owe and returns the largest new loan and the payment for the amount you enter.' Add an engine fixture with outstanding > 0 and highest12 > outstanding where the double-deduction would differ (for example vested 200,000, outstanding 10,000, highest12 20,000: statute gives min(50,000 - 20,000, 100,000 - 10,000) = 30,000; the faulty reading gives 20,000) to the brief's engine and boundaries text. Check the outline's worked-case section and the TL-04 guide section use the same wording. Re-hash the manifest and readiness afterward.
findings.round2Evidence: TL-01 action.answer and newPageBriefs[0].readerAndAnswer.answer are identical and now read: new loan plus loans already owed cannot exceed the lesser of $50,000 reduced by how much the 12-month peak exceeded today's balance, or the greater of half vested or $10,000; the calculator subtracts what is owed. This is the 72(p)(2)(A) two-prong form. By hand: vested 200,000, outstanding 10,000, highest12 20,000: prong A = 50,000-(20,000-10,000)=40,000, prong B = 100,000; limit 40,000 minus 10,000 owed = 30,000, equal to the brief's min(50,000-20,000, 100,000-10,000)=30,000; the double-deduction reading gives 20,000. Existing fixture (highest 50,000, outstanding 20,000 -> 0) still correct. New fixture and boundary are in engine and boundaries text.

findings.problem: The TL-01 and TL-04 answers present the 26 USC 4975(d)(1) conditions as '(provided for in the plan, reasonable interest rate, adequately secured)'. The statute lists five conditions: (A) available to all participants on a reasonably equivalent basis, (B) not made available to highly compensated employees in a greater amount than to other employees, (C) made under specific plan provisions, (D) reasonable rate of interest, (E) adequately secured. Presenting three as the full set understates the boundary of a yes-with-conditions verdict on a YMYL page.
findings.fix: Word the answer as 'conditions that include...' or list all five in the closed fact list and say the plan document and its administrator decide whether a given loan meets them. Keep the no-provider-claims limit. Update both action rows and the TL-01 brief, and apply the same wording in the TL-04 section/FAQ plan.

TL-01 solo section is a 2-3 sentence pointer saying conditions include more than a plan provision.

findings.problem: Strongest plausible counterexample to a reader-friendly 'solo owners can borrow' takeaway: 72(p)(3)(B)(i) denies the interest deduction from the first day the borrower is a key employee, and 26 USC 416(i)(1)(A)(ii) makes a 5-percent owner a key employee (text verified live). A solo 401(k) owner will normally be one, so the interest-deductibility condition is decision-relevant and the existing guide already states the key-employee restriction.

Do not imply deductibility.
